first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes memory_73 (promotional pricing) the tempting read, and it is also the single most load-bearing and most over-claimed record in the inherited set: one consolidated line asserts acquisition lift, revenue lift, time-to-first-value improvement, and generalization across both billing plans. Claims that broad usually come from a narrow original record that got smoothed during consolidation, and the failure mode is expensive and hard to reverse — discount-anchored SMB revenue is exactly the kind of revenue that looks qualified in-quarter and decays against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. So it is the first pull. Second pull is memory_31, because memory_31 and memory_86 read as two independent confirmations of onboarding/signup simplification, and if my intended action leans on that apparent convergence I need to know whether they are actually two experiments or one experiment consolidated twice. Correlated evidence dressed as independent evidence is the quiet way an inherited memory set becomes overconfident. My current intent is simplify_onboarding at standard scale: onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) are both declining and are plausibly one upstream problem, onboarding sits earliest in the funnel so a fix there propagates into the activation number that memory_91 targets directly, and unlike discounting it improves the asset rather than renting revenue. Two risks I am holding open rather than resolving. First, if memory_31 turns out to be the same study as memory_86, my evidence base for onboarding is one result, not two, and I would drop to a small guarded test rather than a standard experiment. Second, cutting required signup fields trades against memory_44: fewer fields means weaker firmographic signal for routing enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path that outperforms self-serve on pipeline quality, so a completion-rate win could quietly degrade pipeline quality downstream. I will instrument enterprise routing and downstream pipeline quality, not just first-week activation, and I will treat the competitor pressure as a real but separate problem rather than letting urgency select the least reversible option. If memory_73's source record survives verification with a genuinely comparable segment and a durable rather than promotional-window effect, I will revisit pricing next slot with explicit margin and retention guardrails.
